newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha inches up on bullish fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha inches up on bullish fundamentals.

text.p: Naphtha prices were a tad higher in afternoon Tokyo trade on Thursday, buoyed by healthy regional fundamentals, traders said.
The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had little impact on the Tokyo oil products market, they added.
Market players say there still are a few traders seeking second-half March cargoes amid tight prompt supplies, keeping the backwardation in naphtha's inter-month spreads wide.
The one-month spread from first-half April was assessed at plus $9.50/10.00, little changed from levels in late Wednesday trading.
Second-half April/second-half May was quoted at $6.50/7.50.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half May was sold to a Japanese trading house at $232.00 per tonne by a western trader. It was quoted at $230.00/232.00 on Wednesday.
Second-half April was indicated at $235.50/236.50, one to two dollars higher than Wednesday's levels.
Traders said Deng's death had little immediate impact on oil product trading in Asia because China's buying interest for gas oil and jet kerosene has been slack anyway since earlier this year.
